mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within the last month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within the last month indicates a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer spending and business investment decline.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the correlation between UNRATE increases and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts over the last two months signals a strengthening demand in the housing market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer confidence and related economic activity improve.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the correlation between HOUST increases and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production by more than 1% within the last month signals a weakening supply side of the economy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as production cuts and inventory adjustments ripple through the economy.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the correlation between INDPRO decreases and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is above 4% and the consumer price index for all urban consumers increases by more than 0.3% in a month, it signals an inflationary environment with tight monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL increase > 0.3% in 1 month
regime_hint: inflationary environment with tight monetary policy
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the joint interaction of high FEDFUNDS and rising CPIAUCSL with negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls increase by more than 200,000 in a month and the unemployment rate decreases by more than 0.2%, it signals a strengthening labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as market sentiment improves.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increase > 200,000 and UNRATE decrease > 0.2% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the joint interaction of PAYEMS increases and UNRATE decreases with positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures over the last three months signals robust consumer demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer spending drives economic growth.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the correlation between RSAFS increases and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production decreases by more than 1% in a month and GDP growth is negative in the last quarter, it signals a supply-side shock, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as production cuts and economic slowdowns impact corporate earnings.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decrease > 1% in 1 month and GDPC1 < 0 in last quarter
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the joint interaction of INDPRO decreases and negative GDPC1 growth with negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
